coptic_restorations.basis: Editor restoration. Relative-future ⲉⲧⲛⲏⲩ 'that comes' opens the chapter's framing clause; line 4 (ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛⲧⲧⲁⲡⲣⲟ) directly continues the verb of motion ('comes forth from the mouth').
Single-letter completion ⲁⲣⲃϩ → ⲁⲣⲁϥ, the Lycopolitan prepositional object 'unto it' governed by ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'hear'. Standard idiom ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ ⲁⲣⲁϥ.
ⲙ̄ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ 'in the ears' completes the standard mouth/ears pairing of the speech-transmission sentence; ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ recurs explicitly in line 17 (ⲙ̄ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ ⲛⲍⲛ ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ).

Five-character noun governing 'of the palate/exchange' that 'draws (the word)' is not constrained by parallels. The five articulators palate-tongue-teeth-lips are visible as the rest of the chain, but the term standing here (whether a sub-part of ⲧϣⲟⲩⲱⲃⲉ or a coordinate organ) cannot be fixed without traces. Honest non-restoration preferred.
ⲥ{4}ⲍϥ̄ across line break = ⲥⲁⲩⲍϥ̄ 'gather it' (Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩϥ̄), a plural-action verb fitting the lips closing/gathering the word. Verb-stem ⲍϥ̄ visible at the start of the next line.
ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲙⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'the five members' — the standard Manichaean formula for the five faculties of articulation, recurring at line 8 (ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲛⲧⲉⲭⲛⲓⲧⲏⲥ) and line 11 (ⲍⲛ +ⲟⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ).
ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'the manner', completing the correspondence-formula ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'according to the manner' — frequent connective in the kephalaia for transition from natural process to its spiritual likeness.
ⲕ{7}ⲉ across line break = ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ 'another'. The next line opens with ⲉ; the form is paralleled three more times in the coin-artisan sequence (ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ in lines 11, 12).
ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ 'another', the third item in the artisan chain; same form as ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ visible earlier in this same line and again in line 12.
Editor restoration. The presentation particle ⲉⲓⲥⲧⲉ 'behold' marks the transition from the enumeration of artisans to the summary statement (ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲛⲧⲉⲭⲛⲓⲧⲏⲥ) that opens the next section.
ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲛⲟⲙⲓⲥⲙⲁ 'their coin' across line break, with ⲛⲟⲙⲓⲥⲙⲁ visible at the start of the next line. The five artisans together form 'their' (collective) coin.
ⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲭⲣⲓⲙⲁ 'serve as a chrēma/currency', completing the Greek loanword χρῆμα — the coin's purpose-clause 'so that it may serve as currency among men'.
ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ 'the word'; ⲙ̄ⲡ visible before the gap and ⲉ after; restoration confirmed by chapter title (ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ⲙⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ) and recurrent ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ throughout.
ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'members'; ⲙ̄ visible before, ⲥ after; recurrence of ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲙⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ throughout the kephalaion fixes this term as the five articulating faculties.
Editor restoration. ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ ⲛⲍⲛ ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ 'ears of some others'; ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ 'others' visible at the start of line 18, completing the closing image of the word being heard by other souls.

english_restorations.basis: Renders ⲉⲧⲛⲏⲩ as the relative-future opener; the next segment continues the verb of motion ('forth from the mouth').
Renders restored ⲙ̄ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ; mouth/ears pairing for word-transmission. Coptic gap {1} (the prepositional ⲁⲣⲁϥ) is absorbed naturally into 'hear it' and needs no English placeholder.
Coptic gap unrestorable; the body-part subject of 'draws' (a 5-character noun governing ⲧϣⲟⲩⲱⲃⲉ) cannot be fixed. English placeholder marked correspondingly.
Renders ⲥⲁⲩⲍϥ̄ 'gather it'; the lips' action of closing upon and gathering the word before it issues.
Renders +ⲟⲩ in ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ (ⲙⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ); 'the five (members)' — the technical formula for the five articulating degrees of the rational.
Renders ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ in the correspondence-formula ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'according to the manner'.
Renders ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ; second item in the artisan enumeration. The English absorbs the line-break naturally rather than mirroring the split letter.
Renders ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ; third 'another' in the chain of coin-artisans.
Renders ⲉⲓⲥⲧⲉ as a presentation particle marking transition from artisan-enumeration to summary statement.
Renders ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩ-, the possessive prefix of ⲡⲟⲩⲛⲟⲙⲓⲥⲙⲁ 'their coin' — the coin produced collectively by the five artisans.
Renders ⲭⲣⲓⲙⲁ (Greek χρῆμα); the coin serving 'as currency' among men, to be received and given in exchange.
Renders ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ 'the word'; the comparison-anchor ('likewise also is this of the word'), which the chapter then unfolds in the following segments.
Renders ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ; 'the five members' — the recurring designation for the articulating faculties.
Renders ⲛⲍⲛ together with the visible ⲕⲉⲕⲁⲩⲉ at the start of the next line; the closing image of the word heard 'before the ears of some others' — souls receiving what has been minted.

restoration_note: The teaching describes how interior truth is articulated outward through the five degrees of the rational (ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲙⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ), figured first as the body's articulators (palate, tongue, teeth, lips, +1) shaping a saying, then as five artisans (ⲡⲓ+ⲟⲩ ⲛⲧⲉⲭⲛⲓⲧⲏⲥ) minting a coin (ⲡⲛⲟⲙⲓⲥⲙⲁ) that becomes currency (ⲭⲣⲓⲙⲁ) of exchange. Almost all gaps are tightly constrained: the recurring 'five members' formula fixes {5} and {13}; the ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲉ-chain in the artisan enumeration fixes {7}, {8}; ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ frames the chapter and fixes {0}, {12}; the mouth/ears pairing fixes {1}, {2}, {14}; standard correspondence-particle ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ fixes {6}; line-break completions fix {4}, {10}; loanword reconstructions fix {11}. Only {3} — a five-character body-part noun coordinate to ⲧϣⲟⲩⲱⲃⲉ — lacks parallels or traces sufficient for a constrained restoration; left unrestored.
